trainers.instruction: Choose all the phrases used to express an opinion.

atoms.b: ++I_think_... ++In_my_view,_... According_to_studies,_... ++I_believe_...

atoms.sound: A recent study from our school’s newspaper shows that the average student spends about two hours a day on social media. What do you all think about this topic?
In my view, social media helps people stay connected with friends and family. It’s nice to see what others are doing, especially when they live far away.
But I believe it also makes people spend less time together in person. I think that makes relationships feel a bit less real.
I also think social media affects mental health. People compare themselves a lot, and that can make them feel stressed or unhappy.

Yes, social media definitely has some problems. For example, people sometimes spend so much time scrolling that they lose track of everything else, and misinformation is also being spread more quickly than ever.
Those are both good points. According to our school newspaper, 41% of students who use social media say they experience poor mental health.

That’s concerning. But I still think social media can be positive. Many people follow mental health or educational pages that help them feel supported and learn new things. Social media can be a good thing if we use it the right way.

atoms.instruction: Who has a negative view of social media?
Who has a positive view of social media?

trainers.instruction: Drag each fact to the student whose opinion it supports.
trainers.hint: Select each student to listen to their opinion.

cats.sound: I believe social media can be harmful because people spend less time together in person and may feel stressed or unhappy.
I think social media is helpful because it lets people stay connected and helps teenagers get access to information about mental health.
I think social media has problems like misinformation and people spending too much time scrolling.

atoms.b: About 38% of teenagers say social media makes them feel anxious or sad.
About 34% of teenagers use social media to learn about mental health.
Over 70% of teenagers use social media to stay in touch with friends and family.
Around 76% of teenagers have seen fake news online in the past year.

atoms.sound: Now that you have stated your opinions, I want you to go and do some more research to support it. Remember, a strong opinion is always one that is supported by facts.
